source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary
source.citation: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (Oxford); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 Hermeneia; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (Oxford, PD); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford); Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition; Reed 2005 Fallen Angels.
source.paleography_note: The layered-witness convention reflects the manuscript-attestation reality: Aramaic DSS fragments are FRAGMENTARY (preserve only portions of chs 1-36); Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus preserves chs 1-32 substantially complete; Ge'ez is the only complete witness but the most distant in time and language from the Aramaic original. Per-verse selection prioritizes the oldest preserved witness; alternate witnesses documented where they differ materially or provide cross-collation value.

verses.text: באדין אדיקו מיכאל ושריאל ורפאל וגבריאל מן שמיא וחזו דמא שגיא די אשתפך על ארעא וכל חמסא דעבד עליה
verses.translit: bě-ʾēdayin ʾaddīqū Mīkāʾēl wĕ-Śarīʾēl wĕ-Rāpāʾēl wĕ-Gabrīʾēl min šĕmayyāʾ wa-ḥăzō děmāʾ śaggīʾ dī ʾištěpak ʿal ʾarʿāʾ wĕ-kol ḥāmsāʾ dī-ʿăḇīd ʿălēh
verses.text_greek: Καὶ τότε παρακύψαντες Μιχαὴλ καὶ Σαριὴλ καὶ Ῥαφαὴλ καὶ Γαβριὴλ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐθεάσαντο αἷμα πολὺ ἐκχυνόμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ πᾶσαν ἀδικίαν τὴν γινομένην ἐπ' αὐτῆς.
verses.text_geez: ወሚካኤል፡ ወገብርኤል፡ ወሱርኤል፡ ወዑራኤል፡ እምሰማይ፡ ሐወጹ፡ ወርእዩ፡ ደመ፡ ብዙኀ፡ ዘይትከዐው፡ ላዕለ፡ ምድር፡ ወኵሎ፡ ዐመፃ፡ ዘይትገበር፡ ላዕሌሃ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iv 6-10 + 4Q202 1 iii 13-15 (Milik 1976 pp. 158, 169-170) — Aramaic preserves all four archangel names
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK + CROSS-CORPUS SITE — THE FOUR ARCHANGELS NAMED.** The four archangels look down from heaven and see the blood and violence. **Aramaic names** (preserved in 4Q201): Mīkāʾēl ('who is like God?'), Śarīʾēl ('prince of God' or 'God is my prince'), Rāpāʾēl ('God heals'), Gabrīʾēl ('mighty one of God'). **Manuscript variation**: the Greek Akhmim reads Σαριὴλ; some Greek witnesses (Syncellus) read Οὐριὴλ (Uriel); the Ge'ez has ዑራኤል (Uriel) in some mss, ሱርኤል (Suriel) in others. The Aramaic ŚRYʾL (Sariel) is original; the substitution Sariel→Uriel is a late transmission shift (Milik 1976 p. 172). **Cross-corpus chain**: this is one of the earliest preserved four-archangels lists in Jewish literature, foundational for the archangelic hierarchy in Tob 12:15, 1 En 20, 3 En, the Hekhalot tradition, and Christian angelology. cf. Dan 8:16, 9:21, 10:13, 21, 12:1 (Gabriel + Michael). cf. Rev 8:2 'seven angels who stand before God.' The four-archangel scheme orients each to a cosmic direction in later Jewish tradition. **LENS-RISK**: the archangelic-hierarchy reading is canon-engagement site — Editor to handle the framing.

verses.text_greek: καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Φωνὴ βοώντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς μέχρι πυλῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
verses.translit: kai eipan pros heautous; Phōnē boōntōn epi tēs gēs mechri pylōn tou ouranou.
verses.text_aramaic: ואמרו דן לדן קל צוחהון על ארעא עד תרעי שמיא
verses.text_geez: ወይቤሉ፡ በበይናቲሆሙ፡ ቃለ፡ ጽራኆሙ፡ ላዕለ፡ ምድር፡ እስከ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሰማይ፡
verses.notes: The cry reaches 'the gates of heaven' — anthropomorphic cosmology of multi-storied heavens with gates (developed in chs 17-36 cosmology + 1 En 72-82). cf. Gen 28:17.

verses.text_greek: καὶ νῦν ὑμῖν, οἱ ἅγιοι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἐντυγχάνουσιν αἱ ψυχαὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων λέγουσαι· Εἰσαγάγετε τὴν κρίσιν ἡμῶν πρὸς τὸν ὕψιστον.
verses.translit: kai nyn hymin, hoi hagioi tou ouranou, entynchanousin hai psychai tōn anthrōpōn legousai; Eisagagete tēn krisin hēmōn pros ton hypsiston.
verses.text_geez: ወይእዜኒ፡ ለክሙ፡ ቅዱሳነ፡ ሰማይ፡ ይስእሉ፡ ነፍሰ፡ ሰብእ፡ እንዘ፡ ይብል፡ አብኡ፡ ኵነኔነ፡ ኀበ፡ ልዑል፡
verses.notes: The humans address the four archangels: 'bring our judgment before the Most High.' The angelic-mediation structure (humans cry to angels who present case to God) is one of the foundational structures of Second Temple apocalyptic — the intermediary cosmology.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ εἶπαν τῷ κυρίῳ τῶν αἰώνων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ θεὸς τῶν θεῶν καὶ κύριος τῶν κυρίων καὶ βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων καὶ θεὸς τῶν αἰώνων· καὶ ὁ θρόνος τῆς δόξης σου εἰς πάσας τὰς γενεὰς τῶν αἰώνων, καὶ τὸ ὄνομά σου ἅγιον καὶ ἔνδοξον καὶ εὐλογητὸν εἰς πάντας τοὺς αἰῶνας.
verses.translit: Kai eipan tō kyriō tōn aiōnōn; Sy ei ho theos tōn theōn kai kyrios tōn kyriōn kai basileus tōn basileuontōn kai theos tōn aiōnōn; kai ho thronos tēs doxēs sou eis pasas tas geneas tōn aiōnōn, kai to onoma sou hagion kai endoxon kai eulogēton eis pantas tous aiōnas.
verses.text_geez: ወይቤልዎ፡ ለእግዚእ፡ ዘዓለማት፡ አንተ፡ ውእቱ፡ አምላከ፡ አማልክት፡ ወእግዚአ፡ አጋዕዝት፡ ወንጉሠ፡ ነገሥት፡ ወአምላከ፡ ዓለማት፡ ወመንበረ፡ ስብሐትከ፡ ለኵሉ፡ ትውልደ፡ ዓለማት፡ ወስምከ፡ ቅዱስ፡ ወክቡር፡ ወቡሩክ፡ ለዓለማት፡
verses.notes: Archangels' prayer addressing 'God of gods, Lord of lords, King of kings.' The triple-title formula is shared with Dan 2:47 (LXX), Rev 17:14 and 19:16 (Christ as 'King of kings'), 1 Tim 6:15. The 'throne of glory' phrase prepares the throne-vision of ch 14.

verses.text_greek: Σὺ πάντα ἐποίησας καὶ πάντων τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἔχεις· καὶ πάντα ἐνώπιόν σου φανερὰ καὶ ἀκάλυπτα, καὶ πάντα ὁρᾷς σὺ καὶ οὐδέν ἐστιν ὃ δύναται κρυβῆναι σε.
verses.translit: Sy panta epoiēsas kai pantōn tēn exousian echeis; kai panta enōpion sou phanera kai akalypta, kai panta horas sy kai ouden estin ho dynatai krybēnai se.
verses.text_geez: አንተ፡ ኵሎ፡ ገበርከ፡ ወእምኔከ፡ ኵሉ፡ ሥልጣን፡ ወኵሉ፡ በቅድሜከ፡ ግሙራዊ፡ ወክሥሙት፡ ወአንተ፡ ኵሎ፡ ትሬኢ፡ ወአልቦ፡ ዘይክል፡ ተኀብዖ፡ እምኔከ፡
verses.notes: Divine omniscience formula — 'nothing can be hidden from you.' cf. Ps 139; cf. Heb 4:13.

verses.text_greek: Σὺ οἶδας τί ἐποίησεν Ἀζαὴλ, ὃς ἐδίδαξεν πᾶσαν ἀδικίαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἀπεκάλυψεν τὰ μυστήρια τοῦ αἰῶνος τὰ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ.
verses.translit: Sy oidas ti epoiēsen Azaēl, hos edidaxen pasan adikian epi tēs gēs kai apekalypsen ta mystēria tou aiōnos ta en tō ouranō.
verses.text_aramaic: אנת ידע מה דעבד אסאל די אלף כל חמסא על ארעא וגלי רזין
verses.text_geez: አንተ፡ ታአምር፡ ዘገብረ፡ አዜኤል፡ ዘመሀረ፡ ኵሎ፡ ዐመፃ፡ ላዕለ፡ ምድር፡ ወከሥተ፡ ምሥጢራተ፡ ዓለም፡ ዘውስተ፡ ሰማይ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q201 1 iv 14-17 (Milik 1976 pp. 158-160) — Aramaic preserves the Asael accusation
verses.notes: **ASAEL ACCUSATION — REVELATION OF MYSTERIES.** The archangels accuse Asael of 'revealing the mysteries of the age in heaven' (Greek ta mystēria tou aiōnos / Aramaic רזין). The 'mysteries' here are the cosmic-knowledge-domains taught in ch 8 — the canon's central interest. cf. Dan 2:18-19, 27-30 (the mystery/rāz terminology). The notion of 'illicit revelation of heavenly secrets' is a key concept — the canon may engage as 'technology-transfer breaking cosmic-information-asymmetry.'

verses.text_greek: καὶ ἐγνώρισεν Σεμιαζᾶς, ᾧ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἔδωκας ἄρχειν τῶν σὺν αὐτῷ ἅμα ὄντων.
verses.translit: kai egnōrisen Semiazas, hō tēn exousian edōkas archein tōn syn autō hama ontōn.
verses.text_geez: ወአስተበቍዐ፡ ሰማይዓዛ፡ ዘለሁ፡ ሥልጣነ፡ ወሀብኮ፡ ይዕገሦሙ፡ ለእለ፡ ምስሌሁ፡ ሕቡረ፡ ይኄልዉ፡
verses.notes: Šemiḥazah accusation: 'you gave him authority to rule over those with him.' The 'authority you gave' is theologically significant — the Watchers' leadership was originally divinely-mandated (consistent with apkallū tradition: the sages were sent to teach humanity). The text presents the abuse-of-mandate.

verses.text_greek: καὶ εἰσῆλθον πρὸς τὰς θυγατέρας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ συνεκοιμήθησαν μετ' αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐμιάνθησαν αἱ θηλείαι, καὶ ἀπεκάλυψαν αὐταῖς πάσας τὰς ἁμαρτίας ταύτας.
verses.translit: kai eisēlthon pros tas thygateras tōn anthrōpōn epi tēs gēs, kai synekoimēthēsan met' autōn, kai emianthēsan hai thēleiai, kai apekalypsan autais pasas tas hamartias tautas.
verses.text_geez: ወቦኡ፡ ኀበ፡ አዋልደ፡ ሰብእ፡ ላዕለ፡ ምድር፡ ወሰከቡ፡ ምስሌሆን፡ ወረኵሳ፡ ወአርአይዎን፡ ኵሎ፡ ኃጢአተ፡
verses.notes: Reprise of the Watcher-human cohabitation. Notice 'they revealed to them all these sins' — knowledge-transfer + sexual transgression are conflated.

verses.text_greek: καὶ ἐγέννησαν αἱ γυναῖκες αὐτῶν τιτᾶνας, ὑφ' ὧν ὅλη ἡ γῆ ἐπλήσθη αἵματος καὶ ἀδικίας.
verses.translit: kai egennēsan hai gynaikes autōn titanas, hyph' hōn holē hē gē eplēsthē haimatos kai adikias.
verses.text_geez: ወወለዳ፡ አንስቲያሆሙ፡ ሬማ፡ እለ፡ በእንቲአሆሙ፡ ኵላ፡ ምድር፡ ተመልአት፡ ደመ፡ ወዐመፃ፡
verses.notes: **The Greek τιτᾶνας 'titans'** — Hellenistic-cultural translation of the gibborim/giants as the Greek mythological Titans (Hesiod, Theogony). This is the strongest direct equation Greek→Greek-myth in the entire Greek Akhmim text. Cross-corpus: cf. Hesiod Theogony on the Titanomachy; cf. the Watchers-as-Titans parallel developed by Justin Martyr + Tertullian in early Christian apologetic.

verses.text_greek: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ αἱ ψυχαὶ τῶν ἀποθανόντων ἀναβοῶσιν καὶ ἐντυγχάνουσιν μέχρι πυλῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἀνέβη ὁ στεναγμὸς αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐ δύναται ἐξελθεῖν ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς γινομένων ἀνομιῶν.
verses.translit: kai nyn idou hai psychai tōn apothanontōn anaboōsin kai entynchanousin mechri pylōn tou ouranou, kai anebē ho stenagmos autōn, kai ou dynatai exelthein apo prosōpou tōn epi tēs gēs ginomenōn anomiōn.
verses.text_geez: ወይእዜኒ፡ ናሁ፡ ነፍሰ፡ እለ፡ ሞቱ፡ ይጠይቁ፡ ወይጸርሑ፡ እስከ፡ አንቀጸ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወዐርገ፡ ገዐሮሙ፡ ወኢይክሉ፡ ወፂአ፡ እምቅድመ፡ ዐመፃ፡ ዘይትገበር፡ ላዕለ፡ ምድር፡
verses.notes: The dead's groan reaches heaven. Persistent theme: even death does not silence the indictment. cf. Rev 6:9-10 (martyrs under the altar crying 'how long?').

verses.text_greek: Σὺ δὲ πάντα οἶδας πρὶν αὐτὰ γενέσθαι, καὶ σὺ οἶδας ταῦτα καὶ ἐᾷς αὐτούς, καὶ οὐδὲ ἡμῖν λέγεις τί δεῖ ποιεῖν αὐτοῖς περὶ τούτων.
verses.translit: Sy de panta oidas prin auta genesthai, kai sy oidas tauta kai eas autous, kai oude hēmin legeis ti dei poiein autois peri toutōn.
verses.text_geez: ወአንተሰ፡ ኵሎ፡ ታአምር፡ እምቅድመ፡ ይኩን፡ ወታአምር፡ ዘንተ፡ ወታኀድጎሙ፡ ወኢትነግረነ፡ ዘይከውን፡ ለክሙ፡ ግቢሮ፡ ሎሙ፡ በእንተዝ፡
verses.notes: Theodicy formula — 'why do you allow this?' The archangels appeal to divine knowledge as a basis for action. Cross-corpus: cf. Hab 1, Pss of lament (Ps 13, 74).
